identification.summary: Storm-0671 is Microsoft's name for a financially motivated ransomware operator listed with the other names UNC2596 (Mandiant) and Tropical Scorpius (Palo Alto Unit 42) [S1][S2][S6]. Mandiant describes UNC2596 as the only cluster it tracks that deploys COLDDRAW ransomware, publicly known as Cuba ransomware [S2]. Coverage of Microsoft's Dec 2022 reporting refers to the Cuba operator as DEV-0671 [S4]; the public sources gathered do not state the DEV-0671 to Storm-0671 rename directly.
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: Exchange exploitation for initial access likely as early as August 2021; an entry on the group's leak site dates to November 2019, consistent with the earliest COLDDRAW samples [S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-0671 (group in development) [S1]. CISA/FBI state the 'Cuba' label is industry shorthand and there is no indication of a connection to the Republic of Cuba [S3]. CERT-UA tracks related activity as UAC-0132 per secondary coverage [S5]. Mandiant reports infrastructure and tooling overlaps with CHANITOR (Hancitor) activity, which are overlaps, not merged identities [S2].

attribution.confidence: No state sponsor is stated in the sources gathered. The group is described as a ransomware operation with multi-faceted extortion [S2][S3]. Secondary coverage notes unconfirmed claims of links to Russian offensive forces and the ransomware reportedly avoids Russian keyboard layouts; these were not verified against a primary source.
attribution.basis: Mandiant clustering of UNC2596 and COLDDRAW use [S2]; FBI/CISA advisory AA22-335A on Cuba ransomware (seen via search results, primary page not opened) [S3]; Microsoft reporting on DEV-0671 as relayed by secondary outlets [S4].

objectives: Financial gain through data theft, encryption and extortion, with stolen data posted on a Tor-based shaming site [S2]. FBI/CISA reported ransom demands and payments rising through 2022 [S3].

sectors: Healthcare and non-profit support organizations (not hospitals, per Mandiant)
Financial services, manufacturing and IT (per secondary summaries)
regions: United States: 65 US and 36 non-US entities compromised as of Aug 2022 per FBI [S3]
targeting.notes: Mandiant saw dozens of victims across more than ten countries [S2]. The FBI count of 101 victims comes via search-result summaries of AA22-335A [S3]. Sector list beyond Mandiant's is thinly sourced.

capabilities.summary: Initial access via exploitation of public-facing Exchange servers (ProxyShell, ProxyLogon), then web shells and the TERMITE in-memory dropper loading NetSupport RAT, Cobalt Strike BEACON and BUGHATCH; credential theft with Mimikatz and WICKER; lateral movement by RDP, SMB and PsExec; BURNTCIGAR kills endpoint security via a vulnerable Avast driver; WEDGECUT enumerates hosts; COLDDRAW encrypts [S2]. Microsoft reported DEV-0671 exploiting OWASSRF (CVE-2022-41080) since at least 17 November 2022 to deliver Cuba ransomware [S4]. FBI/CISA also list phishing, stolen credentials, RDP hijacking, CVE-2022-24521, CVE-2020-1472 and Hancitor as access vectors [S3]. BlackBerry (via secondary coverage) reported a June 2023 campaign adding a Veeam CVE-2023-27532 exploit, with BUGHATCH, BURNTCIGAR, Metasploit and Cobalt Strike [S7].

campaigns.name: Exchange ProxyShell/ProxyLogon intrusions
campaigns.summary: Mandiant assesses UNC2596 likely exploited Exchange vulnerabilities for initial access from as early as August 2021, then deployed web shells and COLDDRAW with data-theft extortion [S2].

campaigns.name: Mandiant publishes UNC2596 / COLDDRAW profile
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports dozens of victims in more than ten countries, about 80% in North America, including utilities and government [S2].

campaigns.name: RomCom phishing against Ukrainian state bodies
campaigns.summary: CERT-UA associated phishing impersonating the Ukrainian General Staff press service and a RomCom backdoor with Tropical Scorpius/UNC2596 (UAC-0132), using hedged wording; Unit 42 and BlackBerry dates conflict in secondary coverage [S5].

campaigns.name: FBI/CISA advisory AA22-335A
campaigns.summary: FBI reports 101 compromised entities (65 US, 36 abroad) as of August 2022, US victims doubled since the Dec 2021 Flash; advisory updated 12-13 Dec with more IOCs [S3].

campaigns.name: OWASSRF exploitation
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reported DEV-0671 using OWASSRF (CVE-2022-41080) since at least 17 Nov 2022 to compromise Exchange and deliver Cuba ransomware; Play ransomware used the same chain against Rackspace [S4].

campaigns.name: Critical infrastructure and Latin American IT integrator campaign
campaigns.summary: BlackBerry (via secondary summaries) reports Cuba operators targeting a US critical infrastructure organization and a Latin American IT integrator, adding a Veeam CVE-2023-27532 exploit [S7].

diamond.adversary: Ransomware operator tracked as Storm-0671 / UNC2596 / Tropical Scorpius, with no state sponsor stated [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Exchange exploitation, TERMITE, BUGHATCH, BURNTCIGAR, WEDGECUT, Cobalt Strike, NetSupport, COLDDRAW ransomware [S2]; OWASSRF [S4]; Veeam exploit [S7].
diamond.infrastructure: BEACON infrastructure used for exfiltration, a Tor shaming site, and contact via email and jabber [S2]. Overlaps with CHANITOR infrastructure and certificates [S2].
diamond.victim: Utilities, government, critical infrastructure and others, mainly North America [S2][S3]; Ukrainian state bodies via RomCom lures [S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Financial extortion; Ukrainian targeting via CERT-UA is hedged and its motive is not established [S5].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing on-premises Exchange servers, Veeam backup servers, RDP and Windows domain credentials [S2][S4][S7].

gaps: No Microsoft primary page for Storm-0671 was found; the DEV-0671 to Storm-0671 rename is not confirmed in sources I could open [S1][S4].
Primary documents not opened: CISA AA22-335A, Microsoft OWASSRF blog (404), Unit 42 Tropical Scorpius report, BlackBerry 2023 report, CERT-UA alert.
No attribution to a state or national origin is established; claims of Russian links are unverified.
Activity after mid-2023 and current operational status were not found.
Relationship between Cuba ransomware, CHANITOR/Hancitor and RomCom operators is only described as overlap or association [S2][S5].
Conflicting dates for Unit 42 first observation of Cuba/RomCom (May vs August 2022) [S5].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing on-premises Exchange servers, Veeam backup servers, and Active Directory credentials are key terrain, as are utilities and government networks in North America [S2][S3][S7]. STEP 2: The group is financially motivated and has no stated state tasking, so it is a criminal threat to DoD-adjacent contractors and critical infrastructure that could degrade mission support [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is public-facing exploit, web shell, TERMITE/BEACON, credential theft, RDP/PsExec lateral movement, EDR kill, exfiltration, then encryption and leak-site extortion [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic ransomware against unpatched Exchange and backup servers, quickly adopting new n-day exploits [S4][S7]. MDCOA is a hit on a defense industrial base or utility supplier timed to disrupt support during a crisis. Candidate indicators: new web shells on Exchange, Avast driver loaded as a service, shar.bat-style share mapping, comps2.ps1 enumeration, unexpected NetSupport installs [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Exchange and Veeam CVE exploitation advisories and feed patch status of mission-relevant servers into the COP [S3][S4][S7]. (2) Authorities: ransomware on contractor or civilian infrastructure is a law-enforcement and CISA/FBI lead; DoD roles are mostly support and DCISE/DC3 sharing, to be confirmed with legal. (3) Mission assurance: protect offline backups and identity systems, since the group targets backup infrastructure and domain credentials [S2][S7]. (4) Coordination: use FBI/CISA IOCs from AA22-335A and share with DIB partners [S3].
